podcast.body: A single from Hybrid Theory, this song originated from the band's frustration with producer Don Gilmore, who was intensely pushing them in the studio. Chester Bennington's lyrics, such as "I cannot take this anymore. I'm saying everything I've ever done before, all these words make no sense" and the chorus "Everything you say takes me one step closer to the edge and I'm going to break," were explicitly directed at Gilmore for dismissing his lyrical submissions. The "shut up" part was also 100% aimed at him. Despite the band's initial reluctance to include it on the album, it was released as a single, became a hit, and effectively launched Linkin Park's career. "One step closer, which is basically Chester Bennington screaming at hybrid theory producer Don Gilmore because Chester was tired of being pushed around in the studio."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This song was cited as one of three Linkin Park tracks that influenced 15-year-old Charles Andrew Williams prior to his school shooting at Santana High School on March 5, 2001. "Williams had been influenced by three different Lincoln Park songs, Papercut, One Step Closer, and In The End."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This was the first official single released by Linkin Park in the summer of 2000. Originally titled "Plaster," it faced critical dismissal as "more of the same old new metal" but resonated with fans for its combination of rapping, scratching, screaming, big riffs, beats, and a catchy, pop-infused sound. "The first proper Lincoln Park single, one step closer, which came out in the summer of 2000."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
